title: 纳德拉如何向员工重申使命、优先级和文化（2025）
topic: 纳德拉如何向员工重申使命、优先级和文化（2025）

source.title: Recommitting to our why, what, and how - The Official Microsoft Blog
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 基于 Microsoft CEO 2025 年发给员工的信；文中对公司业绩、裁员和战略方向的描述均指该历史语境。
paragraphs: Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees this morning.
As we begin a new fiscal year, I’ve been reflecting on the road we’ve traveled together and the path ahead.

Before anything else, I want to speak to what’s been weighing heavily on me, and what I know many of you are thinking about: the recent job eliminations. These decisions are among the most difficult we have to make. They affect people we’ve worked alongside, learned from, and shared countless moments with—our colleagues, teammates, and friends.

I want to express my sincere gratitude to those who have left. Their contributions have shaped who we are as a company, helping build the foundation we stand on today. And for that, I am deeply grateful.

I also want to acknowledge the uncertainty and seeming incongruence of the times we’re in. By every objective measure, Microsoft is thriving—our market performance, strategic positioning, and growth all point up and to the right. We’re investing more in CapEx than ever before. Our overall headcount is relatively unchanged, and some of the talent and expertise in our industry and at Microsoft is being recognized and rewarded at levels never seen before. And yet, at the same time, we’ve undergone layoffs.
translations: 萨提亚·纳德拉（Satya Nadella），董事长兼首席执行官，今早向微软员工传达了以下信息。
随着我们开始新的财年，我一直在反思我们一起走过的道路以及前方的道路。
首先，我想谈谈一直困扰我的事情，以及我知道许多人在思考的事情：最近的裁员。这些决定是我们必须做出的最艰难的决定之一。它们影响了我们曾并肩工作、向他们学习并分享无数时刻的人——我们的同事、队友和朋友。
我想向那些离开的人表达我诚挚的感谢。他们的贡献塑造了我们作为一家公司的面貌，帮助我们建立了今天立足的基础。为此，我深表感激。
我也想承认我们所处时代的不确定性和看似的不一致。从任何客观标准来看，微软都在蓬勃发展——我们的市场表现、战略定位和增长都显示出上升趋势。我们比以往任何时候都在资本支出（CapEx）上投入更多。我们的总人数基本保持不变，而且我们行业和微软中的一些人才和专业水平正以前所未有的水平得到认可和回报。然而，与此同时，我们却进行了裁员。
fullTextParagraphs: Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees this morning.
As we begin a new fiscal year, I’ve been reflecting on the road we’ve traveled together and the path ahead.

Before anything else, I want to speak to what’s been weighing heavily on me, and what I know many of you are thinking about: the recent job eliminations. These decisions are among the most difficult we have to make. They affect people we’ve worked alongside, learned from, and shared countless moments with—our colleagues, teammates, and friends.

I want to express my sincere gratitude to those who have left. Their contributions have shaped who we are as a company, helping build the foundation we stand on today. And for that, I am deeply grateful.

I also want to acknowledge the uncertainty and seeming incongruence of the times we’re in. By every objective measure, Microsoft is thriving—our market performance, strategic positioning, and growth all point up and to the right. We’re investing more in CapEx than ever before. Our overall headcount is relatively unchanged, and some of the talent and expertise in our industry and at Microsoft is being recognized and rewarded at levels never seen before. And yet, at the same time, we’ve undergone layoffs.

This is the enigma of success in an industry that has no franchise value. Progress isn’t linear. It’s dynamic, sometimes dissonant, and always demanding. But it’s also a new opportunity for us to shape, lead through, and have greater impact than ever before.

The success we want to achieve will be defined by our ability to go through this difficult process of “unlearning” and “learning.” It requires us to meet changing customer needs, by continuing to maintain and scale our current business, while also creating new categories with new business models and a new production function. This is inherently hard, and few companies can do both.
But I have full confidence that we can, and we will once again find the resolve, courage, and clarity to deliver on our mission in this new paradigm.
With that context, I want to re-ground ourselves in our why, what, and how: our mission, our priorities, and our culture.

What does achieving our mission look like and feel like for us as a company? When Microsoft is succeeding, the world around us must succeed too. This is why each of us chose to be here, and as a company it’s how we earn our social permission to operate. When Bill founded Microsoft, he envisioned not just a software company, but a software factory, unconstrained by any single product or category. That idea has guided us for decades. But today, it’s no longer enough.

We must reimagine our mission for a new era. What does empowerment look like in the era of AI? It’s not just about building tools for specific roles or tasks. It’s about building tools that empower everyone to create their own tools. That’s the shift we are driving—from a software factory to an intelligence engine empowering every person and organization to build whatever they need to achieve.

Just imagine if all 8 billion people could summon a researcher, an analyst, or a coding agent at their fingertips, not just to get information but use their expertise to get things done that benefit them. And consider how organizations, empowered with AI, could unlock entirely new levels of agility and innovation by transforming decision-making, streamlining operations, and enabling every team to achieve more together than ever before.
That’s the empowerment our mission enables, creating local surplus in every company, community, and country. And that’s our opportunity ahead.
To deliver on our mission, we need to stay focused on our three business priorities: security, quality, and AI transformation.
We are doubling down on the fundamentals while continuing to define new frontiers in AI.
Security and quality are non-negotiable. Our infrastructure and services are mission critical for the world, and without them we don’t have permission to move forward.

We’ve made substantial progress across SFI, QEI, and Engineering Thrive this year, and they remain top priorities to ensure that we continuously improve our innovation velocity and our operational metrics.

We will reimagine every layer of the tech stack for AI—infrastructure, to the app platform, to apps and agents. The key is to get the platform primitives right for these new workloads and for the next order of magnitude of scale. Our differentiation will come from how we bring these layers together to deliver end-to-end experiences and products, with the core ethos of a platform company that fosters ecosystem opportunity broadly. Getting both the product and platform right for the AI wave is our North Star!
Our performance this past year has positioned us well. And we must move forward with the intentionality and intensity that these industry shifts demand.

Growth mindset has served us well over the last decade—the everyday practice of being a learn-it-all, not a know-it-all. It has reshaped our culture and helped us lead with greater humility and empathy. We need to keep that.

It starts with each of us as individuals and our personal drive to learn, improve, and get better every day. Professional rewards, growth, and pride in our craft will always be the prime drivers. Beyond that, we each have the opportunity to connect our personal passion and philosophy of how we derive meaning from the work we do with Microsoft’s mission to empower the world. This is what makes it all worthwhile.

This platform shift is reshaping not only the products we build and the business models we operate under, but also how we are structured and how we work together every day. It might feel messy at times, but transformation always is. Teams are reorganizing. Scopes are expanding. New opportunities are everywhere. It reminds me of the early ’90s, when PCs and productivity software became standard in every home and every desk! That’s exactly where we are now with AI.
Years from now, when you look back at your time here, I hope you’ll say: “That’s when I learned the most. That’s when I made my biggest impact. That’s when I was part of something transformational.”

What we’ve learned over the past five decades is that success is not about longevity. It’s about relevance. Our future won’t be defined by what we’ve built before, but by what we empower others to build now.
And I know that with your dedication, drive, and hard work we can go win together, and change the world in the process.
I look forward to sharing more at Earnings next week and addressing your questions at our next Town Hall.

notes.phrase: shared the below communication with Microsoft employees
notes.meaning: 与微软员工分享以下信息
notes.explain: 这是一种正式的企业内部沟通方式，表示高管向员工传达重要信息
notes.example: The CEO shared the below communication with all staff regarding the upcoming organizational changes.

notes.phrase: reflecting on the road we’ve traveled
notes.meaning: 反思我们一起走过的道路
notes.explain: 使用比喻手法，将公司发展历程比作一段共同走过的路，增强团队凝聚力
notes.example: As we approach our anniversary, let's take time reflecting on the road we've traveled together as a company.

notes.phrase: what’s been weighing heavily on me
notes.meaning: 一直让我深感忧虑的事情
notes.explain: 表达内心沉重感受的习语，表示某事对说话者造成很大心理负担
notes.example: The declining market share has been weighing heavily on the management team lately.

notes.phrase: point up and to the right
notes.explain: 使用图表术语形象描述公司各项指标向好发展
notes.example: Our quarterly results have been consistently pointing up and to the right, showing strong growth momentum.

scenario.title: Explaining two realities during organizational change
english: A teammate asks how the company can be performing well and still be eliminating jobs.

In his 2025 message, Satya Nadella acknowledged the uncertainty and apparent incongruence, then described the need to meet changing customer needs while maintaining current businesses and creating new categories.
You answer without minimizing the job losses or claiming to know more than the message says.
chinese: 一位同事问，公司业绩看起来不错，为什么仍然会裁员。
Satya Nadella 在 2025 年的信中承认这种不确定感和表面上的矛盾，并谈到公司需要在维护现有业务的同时满足客户变化的需求、创造新的品类。
你在回答时不淡化裁员影响，也不声称掌握信中没有提到的信息。

firstAttempt.prompt: 公司宣布调整优先事项后，组员担心现有项目是否还重要。请用英文承认大家会有疑问，说明公告没有交代团队层面的变化，并建议向负责人确认。
firstAttempt.sample: I can see why the announcement raises questions. It explains the broader priorities, but it doesn’t say how our project will be affected. Could we ask our lead what this means for our roadmap?
firstAttempt.rationale: 承认公告引发的疑问，区分总体优先事项与团队具体影响，再提出核实方式。

words.example: The company's fiscal year ends in December, not in March as previously planned.
words.translation: 公司的财政年度在十二月结束，而不是之前计划的三月。
words.note: fiscal特指政府或组织的财政年度，与calendar year(日历年)相对

words.example: The restructuring plan includes the gradual elimination of redundant positions.
words.translation: 重组计划包括逐步淘汰冗余职位。
words.note: 在商业语境中，elimination比layoffs更委婉，表示职位被'消除'而非'裁员'

words.example: There seems to be an incongruence between our stated values and actual practices.
words.translation: 我们宣称的价值观与实际做法之间似乎存在不一致。
words.note: incongruence是较正式的词汇，表示事物之间缺乏和谐或一致性

words.example: Despite the economic downturn, our startup is still thriving with increasing customer acquisition.
words.translation: 尽管经济低迷，我们的初创公司仍在茁壮成长，客户获取量不断增加。
words.note: thriving比successful更强调活力和持续增长的状态

words.example: The company plans to increase CapEx by 20% next year to expand production facilities.
words.translation: 公司计划明年增加20%的资本支出，以扩大生产设施。
words.note: CapEx是capital expenditure的缩写，指用于购买、升级或长期资产的支出

words.example: The department has maintained a stable headcount despite the company-wide hiring freeze.
words.translation: 尽管公司实行招聘冻结，该部门仍保持了稳定的员工人数。
words.note: headcount是商业术语，特别用于统计组织中的员工总数

structure.original: Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees this morning.
analysis: "Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO" 是同位语结构，用于补充说明主语的身份
"shared the below communication with Microsoft employees" 是谓语部分，其中"shared"是谓语动词，"the below communication"是直接宾语，"with Microsoft employees"是介词短语作状语，表示分享的对象
"this morning"是时间状语，修饰整个谓语动词"shared"，表示动作发生的时间
structure.transfer: The leadership team shared the new priorities with department heads yesterday afternoon.

rewrite.bad: The memo changes the company priorities, so we should stop the client project now.
rewrite.good: I can see why the memo raises questions. It explains the broader priorities, but it does not say whether our project should change. Could we ask our lead what this means for the roadmap?
rewrite.translation: 我理解这份备忘录为什么会引发疑问。它说明了更大的优先方向，但没有说我们的项目是否要调整。我们能否问负责人这对路线图意味着什么？
rewrite.pattern: I can see why [message] raises questions. It explains [broader point], but it does not say [specific impact]. Could we ask [person] what this means for [our work]?

cloze.prompt: I can see why the announcement raises ___.
cloze.why: 先承认团队的疑问，再讨论公告实际说明了什么。

cloze.prompt: It explains the broader priorities, but it doesn’t say how our project will be ___.
cloze.why: 区分总体信息与尚未确认的项目影响。

cloze.prompt: Could we ask our lead what this means for our ___?
cloze.why: roadmap 是团队后续工作的路线安排。

dictation.text: Sarah, a project manager at TechNova, was coordinating the launch of a new client portal while her team simultaneously worked on an internal software update.
dictation.why: 听清句中的工作任务、动作和时间信息。

dictation.text: The marketing team demanded immediate changes to the portal's homepage design, conflicting with the development team's tight deadline for the backend integration.
dictation.why: 听清句中的工作任务、动作和时间信息。

translationPractice.prompt: 我理解这项公告为什么会引发疑问。
translationPractice.answer: I can see why the announcement raises questions.
translationPractice.why: 本句练习“I can see why the announcement raises questions.”在承认公告确实让团队产生疑问时的用法。

translationPractice.prompt: 它说明了更大的优先方向，但没有说明我们的项目会受到什么影响。
translationPractice.answer: It explains the broader priorities, but it doesn’t say how our project will be affected.
translationPractice.why: 本句练习“It explains the broader priorities, but…”在区分公告说明的总体方向与未说明的团队影响时的用法。

choice.prompt: 同事看到微软 2025 年员工信中的裁员消息，担心自己的项目是否也会改变。请选出最稳妥的回应。
options: The memo means our project will be cancelled, so we should stop the work now.
I can see why the memo raises questions. It explains the broader priorities, but it doesn’t say how our project will be affected. Could we ask our lead what this means for our roadmap?
The company is performing well, so the layoffs cannot affect any teams.
choice.why: 先承认消息引发的疑问，再区分信中说明的公司层面内容与尚未确认的项目影响。

output.prompt: 部门负责人收到一份新的公司战略备忘录，组员担心现有客户项目是否需要暂停。请用英文承认他们的疑问，说明备忘录只讲了公司层面的优先事项，并建议向负责人确认项目安排。
output.sample: I can see why the memo raises questions. It explains the broader priorities, but it does not say whether our client project should pause. Could we ask our lead what this means for our current roadmap?
check: 是否避免替公司推测项目去留？
是否提出一个明确的核实对象和问题？

credits.audio: 美式英语合成朗读，非公司员工原声。
